claims.text: 58 adults aged 18 to 70 referred with hearing loss or tinnitus; audiology-led community clinic; smartphone otoscope; remote ENT review
claims.quote: New adult otology referrals at a tertiary ear, nose and throat (ENT) hospital aged between 18 and 70 with hearing loss or tinnitus were included. Patients attended an audiology-led community clinic

claims.text: 65% avoided any hospital attendance; 75% pathway shortened by one visit
claims.quote: 58 patients participated. 75% of patients had their pathways shortened by one hospital visit with 65% avoiding any hospital attendances.

claims.text: 95% diagnostic concordance by blinded consultant otologist; 98% satisfied
claims.quote: Electronic validation by a blinded consultant otologist demonstrated a diagnosis concordance of 95% ... 98% of patients were satisfied with the pathway.

claims.text: 24% needed an additional face-to-face appointment for incomplete eardrum views or more examination; 83.3% concordance in 12 with in-person review
claims.quote: 24% required an additional face-to-face appointment due to incomplete views of the tympanic membrane or need for additional examinations ... in the 12 patients who agreed to attend for an in-person review was 83.3%.

claims.text: Judged feasible, safe and non-inferior in the included patient group
claims.quote: This pilot service is feasible, safe and non-inferior to the traditional outpatient model in the included patient group.

claims.text: Topical drops are initial therapy for uncomplicated AOE

claims.text: No systemic antibiotics as initial therapy unless extension outside the canal or specific host factors
claims.quote: clinicians should not prescribe systemic antimicrobials as initial therapy for diffuse, uncomplicated AOE unless there is extension outside the ear canal or the presence of specific host factors

claims.text: Clinicians should distinguish AOE from other causes of ear pain and discharge
claims.quote: clinicians should distinguish diffuse AOE from other causes of otalgia, otorrhea, and inflammation of the external ear canal

claims.text: Guideline target patients are aged 2 years and older
claims.quote: The target patient is aged 2 years or older with diffuse AOE.

claims.text: Reassess if not improving within 48 to 72 hours to confirm diagnosis and exclude other causes
claims.quote: clinicians should reassess the patient who fails to respond to the initial therapeutic option within 48 to 72 hours [corrected] to confirm the diagnosis of diffuse AOE and to exclude other causes of illness

references.notes: Link changed from cureus.com (refused automated reads at audit) to the PMC full-text record. The old '67% of 72,278 patients prescribed oral antibiotics' claim misread a secondary UK study cited in this review (67% was the rate of inappropriate antibiotic choice); that study could not be found on PubMed this run, so the 67% figure was cut and the review's own 6% to 30% finding is used.

claims.text: Oral antibiotics alone in 6% to 30% of primary care AOE patients; amoxicillin and co-amoxiclav most common
claims.quote: oral antibiotics varied between 6% and 30% in patients that were managed only in primary care ... The most commonly prescribed oral antibiotics were Amoxicillin and Co-amoxiclav

claims.text: Seven studies, 31,650 patients
claims.quote: seven studies that were eligible for final analysis, in which 31,650 patients with otitis externa (OE) were assessed

claims.text: Topical antibiotics prescribed for 77% to 95% in primary care; oral choice frequently did not cover typical bacteria; call for better topical prescribing
claims.quote: The rate of topical antibiotic prescriptions was between 77% and 95% ... the choice of antibiotic for empirical treatment frequently did not cover the typical bacteria in AOE. There is a need for improvement

claims.text: Amoxicillin and co-amoxiclav are inactive against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus
claims.quote: the causative bacteria in AOE are predominantly Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus [], and these antibiotics are inactive against these pathogens

claims.text: Inappropriate oral antibiotics risk avoidable adverse effects and antibiotic resistance
claims.quote: Not only ineffective, this practice may also lead to avoidable adverse drug events, non-compliance, antibiotic resistance, and the associated healthcare costs
